IT之家 11 月 24 日消息，OpenAI 今日宣布 GPT-6.2 Sol 正式登陆 ChatGPT 聊天页面，在此前于 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 平台亮相不到一周后，进一步扩大了该模型的应用范围。

根据 OpenAI 官方介绍，此次推出的 GPT-6.2 Sol 针对日常对话场景进行了优化，重点提升复杂请求处理能力，尤其是在用户提供详细指令或要求联网查找信息时，能够更好地理解需求并完成任务。

在具体功能方面，新版模型提升了图像细节识别能力，能够更准确地识别照片中的文字、标签内容以及标志上的符号。在网络信息检索方面，模型也改进了选项比较能力，例如用户在线比较不同商品或服务时，可以根据价格、地理位置等具体条件筛选结果。

此外，GPT-6.2 Sol 还改进了后续交互能力。例如，当用户关注某件商品的价格时，模型可以主动询问是否需要在商品降价时提醒用户。

OpenAI 表示，GPT-6.2 Sol 已于当地时间 11 月 23 日开始面向全球 ChatGPT Plus、Pro、Business 和 Enterprise 订阅用户推送。

与此同时，OpenAI 还公布了旧款模型的退役安排。根据官方公告，GPT-5.6 Sol 将于 12 月 23 日从 ChatGPT 聊天页面、ChatGPT Work 和 Codex 中退役，同一天 GPT-5.6 Terra 也将退出 ChatGPT Work 和 Codex。

OpenAI 表示，随着新模型陆续推出，公司通常会逐步退役落后两代的模型，以释放计算资源，让更多用户能够使用能力更强的新模型。

items.summary: Anthropic 正在从让 Claude 编写代码转向帮助开发人员决定代码何时准备好发布。周一，这家新上市的人工智能公司宣布推出 Claude Ship，这是一套人工智能代理，用于自动进行代码审查、修复和例行代码更改的批准。（来源：TechCrunch·前沿AI与硬件）
items.content:
Anthropic 正在从让 Claude 编写代码转向帮助开发人员决定代码何时准备好发布。周一，这家新上市的人工智能公司宣布推出 Claude Ship，这是一套人工智能代理，用于自动进行代码审查、修复和例行代码更改的批准。

后者是这组新工具中更有趣的部分，因为人工智能编码工具之前已经提供了代码审查功能。 Claude Ship 的值得注意之处不仅在于它可以审查提议的代码更改并识别和解决问题，而且还包括一个代理，可以根据开发团队设置的策略自动批准代码更改。

此次发布正值人工智能编码代理生成大量代码的能力越来越强，从而导致在代码更改上线之前审核和批准方面出现瓶颈。 Claude Ship 的想法是自动化开发过程中涉及的更多工作，主要是将审批权委托给人工智能代理本身。

“大多数团队都希望有人批准每一项更改，当人们编写每一行代码时，这很容易跟上。但现在很多开发人员都与代理一起构建，”公司博客文章解释道。 “在 Claude 代码团队中，Claude 编写了我们的大部分代码，我们希望 PR 之后的所有内容也能如此快速地发展。”

items.originalContent:
Anthropic is moving from having Claude write code to helping developers decide when that code is ready to ship. On Monday, the newly public AI company announced the launch of Claude Ship, a suite of AI agents for automating code reviews, fixes, and approvals of routine code changes.

The latter is the more interesting part of this new set of tools, as AI coding tools already offered code review features before now. What’s notable about Claude Ship is not just that it can review proposed code changes and identify and address problems, but that it also includes an agent that can approve code changes automatically based on policies set by a development team.

The launch arrives at a time when AI coding agents have become increasingly capable of generating substantial amounts of code, leading to bottlenecks in reviewing and approving the code changes before they go live. With Claude Ship, the idea is to automate even more of the work involved in the development process, essentially by delegating approval authority to an AI agent itself.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” a company blog post explains. “On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too.”

Claude Ship is launching in beta, allowing early adopters to use it to review pull requests (PRs), and then decide what’s ready to merge.

The new offering consists of Code Review, which is already generally available, and two new agents now in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward focuses on addressing issues such as failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and feedback from Code Review. It also comments after every push on what it changed and how to roll it back, if needed.

Claude Approvals then applies an approval policy that the team writes as a file in the repository. This approval process can incorporate various signals, including Code Review findings or the company’s own classifiers, with policies written in natural language.

Because the offering is still in beta, Anthropic suggests running the approval functionality in observe-only mode first. Teams can also choose to start with just one repository and set monthly spending limits to have more control over the process.

Anthropic says teams will also still remain in control of where Claude Ship runs, which review settings to use (e.g., Quick, Standard, or Deep), and which changes should be escalated to a human for a decision.

Claude Ship is rolling out to Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub. Code Review is generally available, while PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta.

A handful of tech CEOs, including Elon Musk, are celebrating Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia. Despite being caught in three affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy that has triggered multiple congressional investigations over national security concerns — Huang was reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia on Monday morning.

“The mistake has been corrected,” Tesla and SpaceX leader Elon Musk wrote on X about Huang’s return.

The mistake has been corrected https://t.co/UKvEng9rCD

Musk had been among the most vocal tech leaders to advocate for Huang.

“I think it’s like kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak, and it just doesn’t seem like a good thing for shareholders,” Musk said last week at the DealBook Summit.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman had taken a more neutral stance, commenting last week, “It’s hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen.”

Altman had experienced a similar situation when he was ousted as CEO of OpenAI, then reinstated days later. After the announcement that Huang would return, Altman simply posted, “Jensen!” Many other tech CEOs have similarly refrained from commenting on the matter, given the shifting politics surrounding Huang’s ouster and reinstatement, as well as the national security concerns at the center of the controversy.

In addition to Musk, Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao (CZ), who served prison time for failing to stop criminal activity on the Binance crypto exchange, is also supportive of Huang.

“Glad to see @JensenHuang back,” CZ posted on X with a clapping hands emoji.

Megaspeed, the company that Alice Huang — the woman at the center of the alleged Chinese espionage scandal involving Nvidia — led for over two years, will be placed on a U.S. Commerce Department blacklist, Semafor reported Monday.

The company will be added to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, the outlet writes. This list “contains the names of foreign parties” subject to certain export restrictions designed to ensure that “sensitive technologies do not fall into the hands of those who would threaten U.S. national security or American citizens.”

Functionally, what this will mean is that U.S. companies will not be able to do business with or sell products to Megaspeed without first gaining a special license from the federal government. Semafor cites anonymous sources familiar with the matter to note the move is designed to stop the company “from obtaining US-made semiconductors.”

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based cloud and AI infrastructure provider that, during the period that Nvidia’s boss, Jensen Huang, self-admittedly had an affair with Huang, was one of Nvidia’s biggest chip customers. Last week, the Commerce Department also announced it had launched a criminal probe into the company. Authorities in both the U.S. and Singapore are now probing whether the company defied export restrictions and illegally smuggled Nvidia chips to China. The company has denied wrongdoing.

TechCrunch reached out to the Commerce Department for comment on the reporting and will update this story if it responds.

After lobbying from President Trump, Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday after a short period in which he was ousted by the company’s board over the scandal involving Huang.

An open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without needing to wait for the patch or restarts

OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In a controlled test⁠(opens in a new window), a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart.

We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day.

Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline.

Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running.

Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems.

How the guardian agent observes and protects a running system with eBPF.

OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities:

Live protection: eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system. Security teams can monitor how a proposed shield would affect applications before enforcing it.

Defense at machine speed: OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo to give agents programmable controls to investigate vulnerabilities, develop targeted shields, and validate their effectiveness against exploits and real workloads. Security teams control what gets deployed.

根据网上流传的几段视频，黄仁勋周一回到英伟达办公室，数百名员工鼓掌欢呼。

这位四面楚歌的英伟达创始人本月早些时候因一系列丑闻辞职，其中包括与一名涉嫌中国间谍的丑闻，引发了多次国会有关国家安全的听证会，以及两起与英伟达员工的风流韵事，但在科技界的抵制和唐纳德·特朗普总统的干预后，他被恢复担任首席执行官。

在高呼他的名字后，黄向人群做了简短的讲话。

“谢谢大家给我第二次机会，”他说。 “第二次我将成为一名更好的首席执行官。”

items.originalContent:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.

The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.

After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.

“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”

Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”

Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

Hearing $NVDA employees chant “Jensen! Jensen! Jensen!” as he returned to headquarters today was unlike anything I’ve ever seen in corporate world.This is what we meant when we said Jensen is the Michael Jordan of tech. pic.twitter.com/zSnGEFvVE0

This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well.

Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm.

This thinking isn’t all that fringe. According to one recent poll, 33% of the US public believes AI systems will definitely or probably develop consciousness eventually, and 7% say they already have. In a 2020 survey of 1,092 philosophers, 39% said some future AI systems will be conscious (for comparison, the philosophers were less confident about worms or flies being conscious).

But last week, Anthropic’s openness to the consciousness question came under fire from a rather inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.

Thomas Nagel is best known for a 1974 essay involving a bat. Acknowledging that it’s deceptively hard to define what consciousness is, Nagel offered one way out: we all can see that there is “something that it is like” to be a bat. But the problem is that a bat’s experience of the world—what it is like to navigate via echolocation, for example—is something we cannot actually know. Consciousness is a subjective thing, difficult to define or describe as an outside observer.

You might think this analogy makes it likely that Nagel is open to the idea of AI consciousness. Not at all. In an interview with Wired last week, just after he was awarded the one-million-dollar Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture, Nagel was bluntly critical of the entire idea.

“Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said, referring to those at Anthropic and elsewhere who care about the welfare of AI models.

The gist of Nagel’s view is that we can’t just look at the information processing happening in human brains and AI models while ignoring the physical differences between them—neurons and biology for humans, silicon chips and circuits for AI. There’s no reason to assume that reproducing what a brain does is equivalent to reproducing what a brain experiences.

But it was a screenshot of one of Nagel’s interview responses, in which he said models’ production of language is insufficient to consider them conscious, that got philosophy professors all excited on social media last week. Some called his certainty against AI consciousness “terrible” and “bizarre.” Others came to Nagel’s defense to suggest he meant that being alive is a prerequisite for being conscious, one that AI models do not meet.

Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol to equip its AI support agents with tools and procedures, and GPT‑6 Luna for their conversations.

Beyond knowing how to answer a customer’s request, AI support agents need to be able to execute a solution. And for that, they need access to the right tools and instructions.

According to Richpanel CEO Amit RG, human support agents can use 20 or 30 tools to serve a customer, and the procedures they follow may never have been written down.

Richpanel⁠(opens in a new window) solves that using OpenAI models to both set up the tools and procedures AI support agents need to act and handle customer conversations.

“The intelligence is no longer the bottleneck. It’s everything around it.”

Deploying a support agent often requires a forward-deployed engineer to connect the agent to a customer’s systems and define how it should work. Amit saw that many companies didn’t have engineers to spare and asked himself, “What if that forward-deployed engineer itself was an AI agent?”

So Richpanel built it: an AI manager to handle agent setup. Customers began calling it Boss AI. It writes procedures and defines how Richpanel’s frontline support agent, copilot, and quality-assurance agent call the tools they need.

Richpanel uses GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑6.1 Sol for Boss AI, prioritizing accuracy when building the tools and procedures its other agents will follow.

Richpanel designs the frontline agent to handle hundreds of thousands of conversations, making the cost of each interaction an important part of model selection. It uses GPT‑6 Luna and other OpenAI models for that work. Amit says Richpanel takes the same approach to its copilot and quality-assurance agents.

“What matters is a balance of cost and intelligence,” Amit says. Richpanel’s customers may already use low-cost outsourced support. Automating their operations has to make financial sense against that starting point.

items.title: 【量子位AI】算力周期更迭，数据复合增长：为何存储经济性对中国规模化 AI 至关重要
items.summary: AI 的未来将依赖能够在数据全生命周期中平衡性能、可靠性与经济性的存储架构。
items.content:
AI 的未来将依赖能够在数据全生命周期中平衡性能、可靠性与经济性的存储架构。

随着 AI 应用加速落地，围绕基础设施的讨论仍大多聚焦于算力。尽管对于训练日益复杂的模型及AI大规模应用而言，算力扮演着重要角色，但随着AI实际部署于生产现场，它们所依赖、生成和复用的数据量不断增长，也带来了同样不容忽视的挑战。

与通常在特定周期内运行的计算任务不同，数据在首次使用后的很长一段时间内仍具备价值。企业必须在考量这种不断增长的数据价值的同时，兼顾数据保留的成本，并确保其在未来的工作负载中的可访问性。

随着中国 AI 生态不断扩展，这一转变使存储经济性成为基础设施规划的核心考量。要支持AI的规模化发展，需要构建能够兼顾容量、性能、可靠性和长期成本的基础设施架构。

AI 驱动的数据增长规模，不仅改变了企业需要管理的数据量，也改变了这些数据的使用方式。

在一项由西部数据赞助、IDC 开展的全球研究中，94.7% 的 IT 与业务决策者表示，过去 12 个月中，AI 或生成式 AI 推动了其数据量增长。超过六成的受访者表示数据量增长至少 25%，而 73.8% 的受访者预计，未来三年将出现类似增长趋势¹。

中国尤其清晰地展现了这一增长趋势的演进。截至 2025 年 6 月，中国拥有的高质量数据集数量已超过 3.5 万个，总量超过 400 PB²；到 2026 年 6 月，其总量已超过 1,565 PB³,这反映出用于训练和优化 AI 模型的数据正在迅速扩张。

AI 对数据的需求形态也在发生变化。2025 年，中国推理数据量达到 101.34 EB，并首次超过训练数据⁴。推理数据是指 AI 模型在响应提示、进行预测或执行任务时处理和生成的信息。这表明，中国的 AI 基础设施正在从模型构建阶段迈向规模化运行阶段；在这一过程中，数据需要被持续访问、处理和复用。

这改变了基础设施的考量方式。随着推理在生产环境中持续运行，其生成的后端数据可能在单次响应结束后继续留存，进一步增加企业在 AI 全生命周期中需要管理的数据量。由此，存储成为连接数据与算力的架构的一部分，数据如何存储、访问和移动也变得愈发重要。

AI 的影响不止于数据量增长，还在改变企业如何看待所留存数据的长期价值。AI 系统既会调用大量现有数据集，也会生成合成数据、模型检查点、推理输出和运行日志等新资产。

items.title: 【量子位AI】当大模型接上真实机器人：RoboChallenge Zero首期评测发布
items.summary: RoboChallenge正式发布全新评测基准RoboChallenge Zero
items.content:
RoboChallenge正式发布全新评测基准RoboChallenge Zero

RoboChallenge正式发布全新评测基准RoboChallenge Zero，旨在通过真实机器人任务检验模型的具身零样本能力，并同步公布首批11个多模态大模型在6项任务、330次真机测试中的评测结果。

随着通用多模态大模型在具身相关评测中的表现不断提升，行业内开始出现一种讨论：通用大模型是否会替代专用具身模型，直接承担机器人的理解、决策与操作？要讨论这种可能性，需要先回答一个具体的问题：当大模型接上真实机器人，面对实际的物体、空间和接触关系时，究竟能把任务完成到什么程度？为此，我们推出了真实机器人零样本评测基准RoboChallenge Zero，用测试机器人的方式，检验大模型的具身能力。

首期评测中，我们将11个多模态大模型接入统一的机器人控制接口，在两类真实机器人平台上开展6项操作任务，共完成330次独立测试。结果显示，整体成功率为44.85%，表现最好的模型成功率达到70.00%。但不同任务之间存在显著差异：放置较大积木的成功率为89.09%，书写“Z0”仅为7.27%，在“解开并按要求铺好充电线”的55次测试中，没有一次完整成功。执行效率同样值得关注。即使成功完成积木放置和玩偶抓取，平均也需要约13—14分钟；4次成功的书写任务，平均耗时23.8分钟。这些结果表明，通用大模型已经能够支持部分真实机器人操作，但从理解任务、规划动作，到可靠、高效地完成物理操作，仍有明显距离。

在RoboChallenge Zero中，我们将机器人任务作为考题，让大模型进入真实的感知—推理—行动循环。每一步操作中，模型接收相机画面和机器人状态，并可获取深度、力矩等额外信息，通过工具调用指定机械臂末端的目标位姿和夹爪指令。控制器执行运动后，新的观察被返回给模型，由模型决定下一步动作。我们以机器人是否完整达成任务目标作为主要评判标准，同时单独记录部分进展，区分“做对了一步”和“完成了全部任务”。本期11个模型使用相同的提示词模板与工具接口，每个模型针对每项任务进行5次独立测试。测试之间重置机器人与场景，通过多次真实执行观察系统表现。

放置较大积木是表现最稳定的任务，11个模型中有7个在5次测试中全部成功。这说明，在本次测试条件下，识别目标并完成较为粗粒度的抓取与放置，已经进入多数受测系统的能力范围。修正等式任务则体现了推理能力对操作目标选择的帮助。面对“6＋4＝4”，模型需要移动一根棍条使等式成立。测试中，不同模型找到了不同解法：移动加号中的竖棍，得到“8－4＝4”；或者移动数字6中间的横棍，得到“0＋4＝4”。

但当任务要求精确、连续的运动，以及对物体形态变化的判断时，成功率明显下降。书写“Z0”要求系统把字符要求转化为连续且空间位置准确的运动轨迹。55次测试中，仅4次成功，分别来自GPT-6.2 Astra、Claude Fable 5.2和Gemini 4 Neon。知道要写什么，并不足以保证机械臂能把它准确写出来。

解开数据线的任务困难更加突出，系统需要判断数据线的交叉结构、选择正确的抓取位置，并判断拉动之后的变化。一次看似合理的拉动，可能没有松开绳结，反而将它进一步收紧；每次操作之后，系统还需要重新判断数据线状态。55次测试中，有一次由Gemini 4 Neon驱动的执行成功解开了结，但未按要求拉直，因此获得7分进度分，没有被计为完整成功。

这说明，当前系统能够在部分复杂任务中取得进展，但将这些进展连续组织起来、稳定完成全部目标，仍然存在困难。首期榜单中，GPT-6.2 Astra完成30次测试中的21次，以70.00%的成功率位列第一；Claude Fable 5.2完成20次，以66.67%位列第二。即使是表现领先的模型，也没有在所有任务上保持优势。不同任务上的表现分布，比单一排名更具体地呈现了当前能力的边界。

真实场景中的机器人，需要在持续作业中兼顾成功率、节拍与资源投入。一次任务最终成功，只回答了其中的一部分问题。首期测试显示，成功完成较大积木放置和玩偶抓取，平均需要约13—14分钟，平均Token消耗分别约为48万和51.8万。对于书写任务，4次成功执行平均耗时23.8分钟，平均消耗约173.56万Token，经历43.8次模型调用，接近双臂任务50次调用的上限。在这些任务中，系统通过多轮观察、推理和动作修正逐步接近目标。更多的推理循环可以帮助系统尝试纠错，但也意味着更长的执行过程和更多的资源消耗。

豆包工作把这套能力开放了出来，最近上线的新功能「工作台」，一口气铺开21个专业场景。

从金融投研、创意设计，到医疗、教育，各有各的工作空间，预先配置了相应的技能和工具。

我们挑了金融投研、创意设计、医生和教师四个工作台进行实测，挨个交真实任务，自己看结果。

items.content:
今天凌晨，姚顺雨和腾讯混元团队来到Reddit社区，围绕刚发布的Hy4和Hy4 flash做了一场AMA。

AMA是「Ask Me Anything」的缩写，意思是「有什么想问的，尽管问」。网友在评论区提问，混元团队成员直接回帖。

参与名单上只列了Reddit账号，至于哪个马甲是姚顺雨，我们还没对上号……

11月4日发布的Hy4是旗舰，能理解文本、图像和视频，适合长程软件工程这类需要多步推理、反复调用工具的复杂任务。

11月16日发布的Hy4 flash，主打日常办公的速度和成本。它支持图文输入和最长100万Token的上下文，每个Token激活约120亿参数。

Hy4和Hy4 flash都已接入腾讯WorkBuddy。混元团队还把WorkBuddy里的修表、改文档、做PPT等典型任务纳入了内部评测WorkIndex，按这套评测测算，Hy4 flash的平均单任务成本约为旗舰Hy4的1/20。

两款模型的权重都已公开。到了AMA，有网友直接报出自己的电脑配置：96GB显存、128GB内存，能跑Flash吗？

团队说能跑，主要权重留在GPU上，部分专家层和Engram查表模块可以挪到系统内存。

让Agent自己解题，训练时遇到过什么麻烦？有时它会直接上网找现成答案，跳过解题过程。

还有网友问，后训练里最难改善的行为是什么，团队只回了一个词，Overthinking，过度思考。旗舰Hy4的推理链有时偏长。到了Flash，团队先从旗舰蒸馏，再用强化学习把推理链压短。

items.summary: 量子位·AI与具身智能智库一手报道：Nature：糖尿病大鼠成功恢复正常血糖！用电刺激迷走神经控糖。国内顶尖 AI 智库，深度拆解大模型架构、AI Agent 与具身智能机器人突破。
items.content:
Nature最新研究，新加坡国立大学、南京邮电大学造出了一款植入装置，成功让糖尿病大鼠恢复了正常血糖。

实验结果来看，二型糖尿病大鼠在植入装置仅仅两周后，血糖就降到了接近健康大鼠的水平；而一型糖尿病大鼠则在治疗八周后恢复正常血糖控制，研究人员甚至观察到了胰岛β细胞的增殖和恢复。

这款装置的基本原理是，利用葡萄糖发电，再通过电刺激迷走神经，调动身体原本就存在的神经免疫调节机制，同时根据血糖变化，自动决定启动刺激和停止的时间。

由 Salesforce 联合首席执行官布雷特·泰勒 (Bret Taylor) 联合创立的企业客户体验公司 Sierra 周一表示，已在 F 轮融资中筹集了 17.5 亿美元，使公司估值翻倍至 300 亿美元。此次新一轮融资距上一轮融资不到六个月，该轮融资对公司的估值为 150 亿美元。

新一轮融资由 Greenoaks 和 Lightspeed Venture Partners 领投，领投过前几轮的现有投资者也参与其中，包括 Benchmark、红杉资本、Greenoaks、GV 和 Tiger Global。

企业自动化是人工智能快速采用的少数领域之一。 Sierra表示，目前它为近50%的财富50强公司提供服务，其客户包括纽约银行、汇丰银行、新加坡电信、富国银行、摩根大通、培生集团、Next和Cox Automotive。该公司上月底表示，其基于结果的定价模式帮助其在五个月内将运行收入翻了一番，达到 4 亿美元。

items.originalContent:
Enterprise customer experience company Sierra, co-founded by former Salesforce co-CEO Bret Taylor, said on Monday that it has raised $1.75 billion in a Series F round that doubles the company’s valuation to $30 billion. The new raise comes within six months of its previous round, which valued the company at $15 billion.

The new round was led by Greenoaks and Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors who have led previous rounds, including Benchmark, Sequoia, Greenoaks, GV, and Tiger Global.

Enterprise automation is among the few areas where AI has seen rapid adoption. Sierra said that it currently serves almost 50% of Fortune 50 companies, and its clients include BNY, HSBC, Singtel, Wells Fargo, JPMorganChase, Pearson, Next, and Cox Automotive. The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.

That said, Sierra is working along similar lines as other customer experience players in the market, which is creating a platform to build agents and partner with model developers to provide choices to enterprises. As personal and work agents interact with enterprise systems, Sierra is also working on creating protocol definitions for agents with companies like Meta, Stripe, and Walmart.

Sierra will use the fresh cash build to its technology stack to layer agents for servicing, and hire more sales folks to sign and maintain enterprise contracts faster than its rivals.

Startups operating in the CX space have seen multi-million-dollar rounds come their way with soaring valuations. Voice AI company ElevenLabs is now valued at $22 billion; Decagon is valued at $4.5 billion; Wonderful is valued at $5 billion; and Parloa is valued at $3 billion. Multiple other startups have scored investments of more than $100 million.

During the HumanX conference in Amsterdam in September, Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor argued that despite the popular belief that AI-powered CX companies are replacing humans in contact centers, a majority of its customers are reassigning roles to existing employees.

items.content:
中新网11月23日电 当地时间11月23日，美国总统特朗普在社交媒体发文，祝贺英伟达董事会决定恢复黄仁勋担任公司首席执行官。

特朗普表示，英伟达董事会作出了“正确且恰当的决定”。他称，美国需要黄仁勋领导英伟达，以确保不仅是公司自身，也包括美国经济的成功与繁荣。

特朗普还表示，美国政府没有理由认为黄仁勋重返英伟达会带来国家安全风险。美国司法部长已确认，美国政府没有证据表明黄仁勋从事过任何违法行为。

特朗普还称，自己已经与黄仁勋有所接触，并称赞他是“一位伟大的爱国者，也是美国的宝贵财富”。

不过，特朗普同时强调，英伟达仍应继续开展全面的内部调查，审查公司是否遵守美国出口管制规定，以确保履行法律义务，并承担保护美国国家安全的责任。

当天，英伟达宣布，董事会一致投票决定，即日起恢复黄仁勋担任公司总裁兼首席执行官及董事会成员职务。公司表示，董事会在听取美国政府高层意见后，认为黄仁勋复职不会带来国家安全风险。

items.content:
中新网11月23日电 当地时间11月23日，英伟达在官网发布声明称，公司董事会一致投票决定，即日起恢复黄仁勋担任公司总裁兼首席执行官及董事会成员职务。

英伟达表示，董事会在与黄仁勋进行一系列讨论和会面后，对其坦诚程度及领导英伟达的能力表示认可。董事会在作出决定过程中还听取了美国政府高层的意见，并据此确信，恢复黄仁勋职务不会带来国家安全风险。

英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示，董事会认为黄仁勋是领导英伟达的合适人选，其复职符合公司股东、员工、合作伙伴及客户的最佳利益。此前担任临时首席执行官的科莱特·克雷斯将继续担任公司首席财务官，哈维·琼斯则继续担任董事会主席。

黄仁勋在声明中表示，很荣幸能够重返英伟达，并将以谦逊的态度和更坚定的承诺承担领导责任。他感谢董事会的信任，以及公司管理团队、员工、股东和全球合作伙伴在此期间给予的支持。

In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.

The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.

Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 am ET.

In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. A long list of high-profile tech executives have also pushed the board to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.

The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”

Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.

Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”

In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
